Defence Holdings PLC
10 September 2026
10 September 2026
London, UK
Defence Holdings Provides Operational and Strategic Business Update
Defence Holdings PLC (LSE: ALRT), the UK's software-led defence technology group, today provides investors and shareholders with an operational update ahead of the Company's Annual General Meeting on 22 September 2026, providing further detail on the continued execution of its Operating Model through updates on ongoing project delivery, commercial contracts, the development of its sovereign software capabilities and product ecosystem, and the expansion of its Investment Pillar. Operational updates of this nature will now be delivered on a quarterly basis.
Highlights
● First UK Ministry of Defence contract continues to progress through delivery, with three priority use cases identified and completion remaining on track for October 2026.
● Second UK Ministry of Defence customer engagement has advanced materially, with contracting discussions progressing and the Company continuing to expect the contract to be secured in the near term.
● Sovereign software product ecosystem expands further, with the Company's fourth and fifth products now in active development following the identification of additional customer problem sets.
● Defence Fund investment pipeline expands to nine opportunities, with three having progressed to an advanced stage of discussion and engagement with prospective third-party investors.
● Defence Holdings and Whitespace to mark twelve months of their strategic partnership, with a recorded discussion between the companies' Chief Executives to be published on 15 September 2026.
Operational Update
This operational update comes at a time when Defence Holdings is making significant progress in the execution of its Operating Model across multiple strategic activities. In recent weeks, the Company announced the activation of the Investment Pillar of its Operating Model through the launch of the Defence Fund and, earlier this week, the formal commencement of the Meridian Accelerator Programme, introducing the ten companies selected for its inaugural cohort and the technologies and customer problem sets they have the potential to address across UK Defence.
Alongside these developments, the Company has continued to make progress across its commercial activities, including the active delivery of its first UK Ministry of Defence contract under Project Strong, the progression of a second anticipated Ministry of Defence engagement and the continued development of its broader commercial pipeline. The following update provides investors and shareholders with further detail on these activities, together with progress across the Company's sovereign software capabilities, strategic investment activities and defence technology ecosystem, ahead of its Annual General Meeting on 22 September 2026.
Customer & Commercial Update
First UK Ministry of Defence Contract
Delivery of the Company's first UK Ministry of Defence contract continues to advance, with the programme remaining on track for completion in October 2026.
Three priority use cases have now been identified in collaboration with the customer, with delivery progressing through a series of agile development sprints. Relevant end-user groups are actively engaged in developing representative operational scenarios, which are being incorporated into the capability to assess performance against each use case and inform further development and refinement.
This next phase of delivery will provide further validation of the capability against identified customer requirements ahead of the scheduled completion of the initial pilot in October.
Second UK Government Contract
The Company continues to progress contracting discussions in relation to the second customer engagement with the UK Government referenced in its previous updates to the market.
These discussions have advanced materially since the Company's last update and there has been no change to the anticipated scope or structure of the engagement. The Company continues to expect the contract to be secured in the near term.
The proposed engagement is expected to comprise an initial four-month pilot, structured similarly to the Company's first UK Ministry of Defence engagement. Subject to completion of the contracting process, delivery is expected to commence immediately thereafter, with the Company working directly with customer stakeholders through the initial pilot period.
Commercial Pipeline
Alongside its existing customer delivery activities, the Company is actively developing a broader pipeline of commercial opportunities across UK Defence and allied markets.
Within the UK Ministry of Defence, Defence Holdings is working across a broader range of stakeholders to identify opportunities for further design partnerships, applying the customer-led approach established through Project Strong to additional operational requirements and capability areas. The Company is also progressing discussions with private sector organisations around partnership models that combine Defence Holdings' sovereign software capabilities and commercial platform with complementary technologies, expertise and customer relationships when engaging with UK Ministry of Defence end users.
In parallel, work is underway to establish routes through which the Company's sovereign software products can be brought to market in allied jurisdictions, extending the commercial opportunity beyond the UK. Together, these activities are creating multiple routes through which the Company's commercial pipeline can develop, with the immediate focus on converting this engagement into defined customer opportunities, new partnerships and further contracted activity.
Defence Holdings and Whitespace Strategic Partnership Update
On 15 September 2026, Defence Holdings will mark twelve months of its strategic partnership with Whitespace through the publication of a recorded discussion between Defence Holdings Chief Executive Officer Andrew Roughan and Whitespace Chief Executive Officer Paul Jenkinson.
The discussion will reflect on the development of the partnership over its first year and how the relationship has expanded across customer delivery, sovereign software capability development and the broader national security landscape.
It will provide further detail on the evolution of Project Strong and the role of the Gloucestershire Police AI trial in developing capabilities with potential application across the national security landscape, while exploring how Defence Holdings' commercial platform and Whitespace's engineering expertise are being brought together to support the continued development and commercialisation of sovereign software capabilities.
Looking ahead, Andrew Roughan and Paul Jenkinson will outline the next phase of the partnership, including the companies' participation at the Emergency Services Show in Birmingham on 16 and 17 September 2026 and the opportunities being pursued across defence, law enforcement and the wider national security market.
Fourth and Fifth Sovereign Software Products in Active Development
The Company's sovereign software product ecosystem continues to expand, with progress across Project Strong, Ixian and the Gloucestershire Police ROTI / ROVI project now directly informing the next phase of product development.
Discovery sessions with customers and end users have identified additional and distinct problem sets where Defence Holdings can apply its sovereign software capabilities. These requirements have led directly to the scoping and development of what will become the Company's fourth and fifth sovereign software products. Both are now in active development, further extending the Product pillar of the Defence Holdings Operating Model, with further details on both products to be announced before the end of September 2026.
The development of Products 4 and 5 demonstrates the increasingly customer-led nature of the Company's product strategy, with engagement around existing capabilities providing a direct route to identifying further requirements and translating them into new sovereign software products.
Alongside the technologies and capabilities brought into the Defence Holdings ecosystem through Meridian, the expansion of the Company's own product portfolio has materially increased the breadth of requirements it can address across defence and national security.
Development of the Defence Holdings PLC Operating Model, Investment Pillar
As outlined within the Company's Operating Model, Defence Holdings intends to create long-term shareholder value through both the commercialisation of sovereign software capabilities and selective participation in the growth of strategically relevant defence technologies. Following the activation of the Investment Pillar through the launch of the Defence Fund, the Company continues to build momentum across both strategic investment activities and the development of a growing pipeline of opportunities originating from its wider defence technology ecosystem.
Defence Fund
Since establishing the Defence Fund, the Company has made significant early progress in developing both its investment pipeline and third party investor base. Nine investment opportunities are now under active consideration, with three having progressed to a more advanced stage of engagement.
The businesses currently being considered represent a high-calibre group of defence technology companies operating across areas closely aligned with the future requirements of the UK and its allies. While reflecting many of the same technology areas and operational requirements being addressed through Meridian, the Fund's pipeline is focused on businesses at a later stage of maturity, with established technologies, commercial traction and clearer pathways to scale. This gives Defence Holdings access to opportunities across different stages of the defence technology lifecycle, from emerging companies identified through Meridian through to more established businesses capable of supporting larger-scale investment.
Engagement with prospective third-party investors progresses positively. The Company is taking a considered approach to the development of the Fund's investor base, focused on bringing together the right combination of capital, sector understanding and strategic alignment to support both the Fund and the businesses in which it invests.
The progress being made across both sides of the Fund, developing a high-quality pipeline of investable businesses while building the appropriate capital base around them, continues to strengthen the foundations for its deployment.
Strategic Equity Positions
The Company's strategic equity position in OM Defence Systems has helped further develop its framework for using strategic equity, including success-based sweat equity, to participate in the growth and commercial development of businesses across the defence technology ecosystem.
Building on this approach, the Company is progressing a number of opportunities where its capabilities, expertise, customer access and commercial support can be combined with strategic equity participation. These opportunities are emerging from the Company's broader defence technology ecosystem, with a focus on businesses and technologies aligned with Defence Holdings' wider strategic and commercial objectives.
This approach reflects the Company's broader Operating Model and provides two complementary routes to value creation: generating commercial value through the deployment of Defence Holdings' capabilities and platform, while establishing strategic equity exposure to businesses where the Company can contribute directly to their growth and commercial progression.
Meridian Ecosystem Development
Following the formal commencement of the Meridian Accelerator Programme on 1 September 2026, Defence Holdings earlier this week introduced the ten companies selected for its inaugural cohort, showcasing the technologies they are developing and the priority customer problem sets they have the potential to solve across UK Defence.
With the programme now underway, the Company's focus has turned to the continued development of the Meridian ecosystem, broadening the range of strategic partners capable of supporting cohort members whilst creating additional pathways to customers, technical collaboration and strategic investment.
The quality of applications received for the inaugural cohort also demonstrated the depth of innovation emerging across the UK defence technology sector. Whilst places within the first cohort were necessarily limited, Defence Holdings intends to remain engaged with a number of applicants to explore future opportunities for collaboration across its wider ecosystem, recognising that Meridian is intended to become a long-term platform connecting innovative businesses with customers, strategic partners and investment opportunities.
Annual General Meeting
The Company's Annual General Meeting will be held on 22 September 2026.
The Board looks forward to updating shareholders on the progress outlined in this announcement and providing further insight into the continued execution of Defence Holdings' Operating Model. Shareholders are encouraged to attend and details relating to the meeting are available in the Notice of Annual General Meeting previously circulated by the Company, and available at www.defenceplc.com/investors/.
Defence Holdings Chief Executive Officer, Andrew Roughan
, commented
"After five months as Chief Executive Officer, I am delighted with the progress we have made against the Operating Model we set out for Defence Holdings, focused on building valuable defence technology ecosystems, developing and commercialising sovereign intellectual property, and creating multiple routes to participate in the value generated across them. We are now seeing that model translate into tangible activity. Meridian is building an ecosystem around emerging UK defence technologies, while OM Defence Systems and our cornerstone position in the Defence Fund are creating opportunities to establish equity exposure to high-potential businesses.
Through our Product Studio, we are developing sovereign intellectual property both wholly owned and collaboratively, with our fourth and fifth products now in active development. Our first UK Ministry of Defence contract is progressing towards completion, while discussions around our anticipated second customer engagement have advanced materially. Through our Open Source Prime model, we are also building the commercial pathways through which technologies from across our ecosystem can reach defence customers.
In a relatively short period of time, we have moved Defence Holdings from an idea, to a defined strategy, to an operational business with customers, products, strategic equity positions and an expanding defence technology ecosystem. As we approach our AGM, I am excited by the progress we have made and the significant long-term growth opportunity ahead."
Defence Holdings Chief Technology Officer, Andy McCartney,
commented:
"I have spent my career working at the leading edge of technology and defence, and the circumstances we face today are both unique and increasingly complex. The nature of the threats, the pace of technological change and the complexity of the problems that need to be solved underline how seriously we must approach the development and investment in the next generation of defence capability.
"Defence Holdings has created an approach designed for that environment. We are building an ecosystem where promising, agile and disruptive companies can develop alongside our own sovereign software capabilities, while working with customers and strategic partners to address some of the hardest problems that remain unsolved.
"We can already see that approach working. Direct engagement with customers and end users is shaping our product roadmap and has led to our fourth and fifth sovereign software products now entering active development, while Meridian has significantly broadened the technologies and capabilities accessible through our wider ecosystem.
"I often talk about the need to operate on a 'wartime footing'. For me, that means moving with urgency, working collaboratively and focusing our technology on the problems that matter most. I am proud that this is the approach Defence Holdings is taking, and of the progress our teams and partners are making."

latest.content:

Defence Holdings PLC
08 September 2026
8 September 2026
London, UK
Defence Holdings Announces Inaugural Meridian Cohort
Defence Holdings PLC ("Defence Holdings", "DH" or the "Company"), the UK-based defence technology company focused on delivering sovereign software capabilities for the UK and its allies, is pleased to announce the ten companies selected to participate in the inaugural cohort of Meridian, the Company's defence technology accelerator programme.
The inaugural cohort brings into the Defence Holdings ecosystem a new range of technologies and capabilities addressing identified requirements across defence and national security. Through Meridian, the Company will work alongside each cohort member to accelerate the development of these capabilities, strengthen their connection to operational requirements and create clearer pathways towards customers, deployment and commercial opportunities.
The programme formally commenced on 1 September 2026 and is now in active delivery with its inaugural cohort.
Highlights
●
Ten companies selected to participate in Meridian's inaugural cohort, bringing a broad range of technologies and capabilities addressing identified requirements across defence and national security into the Defence Holdings ecosystem.
●
Cohort combines emerging technologies with existing commercial and operational traction, including UK Ministry of Defence contracts, NATO and allied defence deployments, established commercial revenues and customer pipelines.
●
Selected companies span areas of growing strategic importance including autonomous systems, resilient communications, AI assurance, intelligence, information warfare, electronic warfare, maritime security and critical infrastructure protection, with several of these areas receiving significant UK Government defence investment.
●
Meridian provides Defence Holdings with earlier and deeper access to emerging defence technologies, creating opportunities for collaboration, technology integration, joint customer engagement, commercial partnerships and, where appropriate, strategic investment.
●
Meridian formally commenced on 1 September 2026 and is now in active delivery, with initial deep-dive sessions underway and individual technical, commercial and customer roadmaps being developed for each cohort member.
Selection of the Inaugural Cohort
The selection process for Meridian's inaugural cohort attracted an exceptionally strong response from across the UK technology ecosystem, both in the volume of applications received and the quality of the businesses and technologies represented. Applications spanned a broad range of capabilities relevant to defence and national security, creating a highly competitive selection process for the ten companies ultimately chosen to form the inaugural cohort.
Applications were reviewed through a structured selection process led by Defence Holdings PLC, with the selection committee comprising members of the Company's broader team together with representatives from Meridian's partner ecosystem, including Oracle and IMSL.The composition of the committee ensured that each application was assessed from multiple perspectives, combining technical scrutiny with an understanding of operational defence requirements, commercial potential and the practical pathways required to move emerging technologies towards deployment.
Companies were assessed against a range of criteria, including the relevance of their technology to identifiable defence and national security problem sets, technical differentiation and maturity, potential pathways towards operational deployment, scalability, sovereign capability and the strength of the team responsible for its development. Particular emphasis was placed on technologies where Meridian's combination of defence relationships, technical expertise and strategic partners could provide a meaningful opportunity to accelerate progress.
The ten companies ultimately selected bring together a diverse range of technologies and capabilities aligned to areas of growing importance across defence and national security. The cohort combines emerging technologies with businesses already demonstrating commercial and operational traction, including UK Ministry of Defence contracts, NATO and allied defence deployments, established commercial revenues and customer pipelines. Collectively, they reflect Meridian's focus on identifying technologies with clear relevance to current and emerging operational requirements, together with a credible pathway towards practical application and commercial adoption.
Inaugural Cohort Members
A short overview of each of the ten companies selected for Meridian's inaugural cohort is provided below in alphabetical order. Further information on each cohort member can be found at
meridianbydefenceplc.com
.
1. Blackmoor Defence
Blackmoor Defence is developing technologies designed to provide greater visibility into parts of the operating environment that are often invisible to the operator, built around distributed sensing, secure evidence, data fusion and operator decision support. Its technologies span RF and GNSS integrity awareness, autonomous-system assurance, maritime security and critical-infrastructure protection, with the company currently estimating SCOUT at TRL 5, SALT at TRL 2 and Sea Sentinel at TRL 7. Together, Blackmoor's technologies provide Meridian with capabilities spanning electronic warfare awareness, autonomous-system assurance, maritime security and critical-infrastructure protection, with technologies that can be shaped around identifiable defence requirements.
2. CulturePulse
CulturePulse develops population-scale behavioural simulation technology designed to model how people form beliefs, react to events and respond to policies, narratives and external interventions, providing decision-makers with a way to test how groups may respond before an intervention is made. Its technology has analysed more than 200 million personas and run more than two million simulations, with the founding team having raised €85 million in grant funding over the course of their careers, alongside validation through work involving NATO, the United Nations and UK Government.. By allowing different courses of action and communications strategies to be explored in simulation rather than first tested against a live population, the technology can help decision-makers understand how people may respond to an intervention and how that response could be altered.
3. Haziel
Haziel is a frontier research lab building AI to support missions in contested environments. Its first product, Godwit, uses autonomous weather-based navigation to hold High Altitude Balloons over a fixed location, creating resilient communications and PNT infrastructure independent of conventional ground networks and space-based systems. Haziel's AI is trained on 1PTB of weather data and 4BN rows of EW data, with the technology completing a six-day simulated station-keeping demonstration in Colorado in May 2026 at approximately 18.5 kilometres altitude. As military forces become more distributed and more dependent upon data, they are increasingly exposed to jamming and GNSS-denial, creating applications across resilient tactical communications and PNT, satellite backup, persistent intelligence, surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR
)
relay, autonomous-system backhaul, border monitoring and temporary regional communications.
4. Inexorable
Inexorable is a UK defence technology company developing a sovereign software orchestration layer for coordinating large teams of uncrewed autonomous vehicles. Its AI platform operates across air, land and maritime environments and is designed to sit across third-party vehicles and mission systems. This enables heterogeneous fleets to share information, replan missions and coordinate activity without being tied to a single hardware provider. Its technology has demonstrated control of more than 100 uncrewed vehicles in simulation, and the company has been awarded three UK Ministry of Defence contracts between December 2025 and August 2026. The capability is closely aligned with the UK's Strategic Defence Review, which identifies autonomy, AI and uncrewed systems as central to the future Integrated Force and calls for their incorporation in high numbers over the coming years.
5. Marlin Intelligence
Marlin Intelligence is developing a biomimetic soft-robotic uncrewed underwater vehicle for surveillance and sensing in shallow and contested littoral environments. The platform uses an elastomeric body and biomimetic actuation, with the objective of reducing its visual and acoustic signature. It is designed for autonomous or remotely controlled operation, deployment individually or in swarms. Naval forces are increasing their use of uncrewed and autonomous systems, while the protection of ports, naval facilities, cables, pipelines and other subsea infrastructure has become a more prominent national-security priority. These requirements create demand for affordable sensing systems that can be deployed in numbers and operate persistently in complex coastal environments, with potential application across surveillance, infrastructure protection, mine countermeasures and submarine tracking. Marlin Intelligence is also a member of the Oracle Defense Ecosystem.
6. Nisien
Nisien is a Welsh technology company developing HERO, an AI-driven early-warning platform for detecting, classifying and prioritising online threats, including text and imagery generated or manipulated using AI, alongside misinformation, abuse and related threats. Generative AI makes it increasingly easy to create convincing text and imagery that can misrepresent events, spread misinformation or influence operational decision-making, creating a growing requirement to identify deceptive content quickly and establish what can be trusted. The technology originates from more than a decade of academic and applied research associated with Cardiff University and is already being commercialised, including a multi-year recurring contract. Its defence-market modelling identifies applications including AI-modified document scanning and content verification, illustrating how the underlying technology could extend beyond social monitoring into wider information-assurance requirements.
7. N:SYM
N:SYM is a Manchester-based AI company developing BeliefNet, a proprietary neuro-symbolic AI architecture designed for high-consequence environments where decisions need to be explainable, assured and auditable. BeliefNet combines neural-network methods with symbolic logic, producing predictions alongside an explicit reasoning chain that allows users to understand the factors supporting or contradicting an outcome. Applications identified by the company include intelligence prioritisation, sensor interpretation, explainable threat classification, mission decision support and autonomous-system assurance. These are environments where the speed of machine analysis can provide significant advantage, but where human accountability remains essential. N:SYM's low-compute approach could also allow AI to be deployed closer to the point of decision, including environments where access to cloud infrastructure or high-performance computing is constrained.
8.
TACTIQL
TACTIQL is a Canadian defence technology company developing the software infrastructure required to make information generated by different military sensors and systems interoperable. Its FULCRUM platform ingests multiple data formats, processes and standardises them, converts information into recognised military and commercial standards and distributes it across networks and command-and-control systems. TACTIQL is already operational, bootstrapped and cash-flow positive. Its technology has been baselined on the Canadian Army's mission network supporting NATO's Enhanced Forward Presence in Latvia, has supported Canadian Navy uncrewed-system integration and has been deployed at NATO and coalition exercises including CWIX and REPMUS. The company reports TRL 9+ validation by Canada and NATO and participation in NATO DIANA Phase II. TACTIQL is also a member of the Oracle Defense Ecosystem.
9.
Unified UV
Unified UV is building the physical coordination infrastructure that turns autonomous platforms into coordinated teams. The company's plug-and-play onboard hardware module uses directional links to provide resilient mesh communications, determine relative positions and maintain synchronised timing, without relying on GNSS, conventional communications or manual direction. No single autonomous platform will determine future military advantage. The decisive capability will be the ability to combine multiple systems into coordinated teams that can share information, allocate tasks and adapt at machine speed. As the UK expands its use of drones and autonomous systems, every additional platform increases the need for resilient infrastructure that can connect the force at scale. Unified UV is addressing this foundational requirement: enabling diverse autonomous assets to be fielded not simply as a collection of individual platforms, but as a coherent fighting system.
10. Valinor Intelligence
Valinor Intelligence is an intelligence-as-a-service company combining proprietary OSINT technology with a distributed community of more than 300 verified analysts and subject-matter experts. Valinor combines automated collection with specialist intelligence analysts to deliver on demand, completed intelligence products, monitoring and bespoke datasets, providing surge specialist analytical capability when and where it is required. The proliferation of commercially available data has changed the economics of intelligence, creating applications across defence, national security, critical infrastructure, geopolitical risk and commercial intelligence. Valinor enters Meridian with an established commercial base rather than a purely prospective market case, with reported closed-won business of over thirty deals and a qualified sales pipeline worth over £7 million.
Oracle Defense Ecosystem
The strategic relationship between Defence Holdings and Oracle continues to deepen through Meridian, creating increasingly strong connections between the two organisations' defence technology ecosystems. The presence of two Oracle Defense Ecosystem members within Meridian's inaugural cohort provides an early demonstration of that alignment.
Bringing these ecosystems closer together expands access to technologies, technical expertise, defence relationships and potential customers, creating stronger pathways through which emerging capabilities can progress towards commercial and operational opportunities.
For Defence Holdings, this growing relationship with Oracle strengthens the reach of Meridian beyond the programme itself, creating further opportunities for customer access, technology collaboration and commercial activity across the UK and allied defence markets.
Programme Delivery Underway
Meridian formally commenced on 1 September 2026 and has now entered active delivery with its inaugural members.
Initial deep-dive sessions with cohort members are underway, focused on developing a detailed understanding of each company's technology, current stage of development, commercial objectives and the operational defence requirements against which its capability can be applied.
These sessions will inform the development of individual roadmaps for each cohort member, identifying the technical, commercial and customer milestones that will form the focus of their participation in Meridian. This will include opportunities for customer engagement, technical validation, strategic partnerships and routes towards operational deployment.
As these roadmaps develop, Defence Holdings will work with cohort members and Meridian's wider partner ecosystem to accelerate progress against these priorities and identify opportunities where the Company's relationships, capabilities and access to the defence market can support their commercial development.
Andrew Roughan, Chief Executive Officer of Defence Holdings,
commented:
"The quality of the companies selected for Meridian's inaugural cohort reflects the strength of the technology being developed across the UK defence ecosystem and the scale of the opportunity to connect that innovation more effectively with operational requirements.
"Selection is only the starting point. Meridian is now in active delivery and our focus is on working with each of these companies to understand where their technology can have the greatest operational impact, develop clear roadmaps and accelerate their progress towards customers, deployment and commercial opportunities.
"For Defence Holdings, Meridian significantly expands the range of technologies and capabilities within our ecosystem. It gives us earlier access to companies addressing some of the most important requirements across defence and national security, while creating opportunities to bring together our customer relationships, technical capabilities and strategic partners around those technologies.
"We have assembled an exceptional inaugural cohort and I am excited about what we can build with these companies as the programme progresses."
Further to this announcement regarding the inaugural Meridian cohort, the Company will provide a separate operational update in the coming days
